samples.question: The picture shows one thin wire folded into a staircase of eight straight runs on a plain background. The runs alternate between horizontal and vertical, so the wire turns a right angle between one run and the next. One end of the wire is marked by a small solid square block; the other end is bare. Walk along the wire starting from the blocked end: the straight run that touches the block is run one, the run after the first turn is run two, and so on up to run eight at the bare end. The length of a run is how far the wire travels along that straight run, and horizontal and vertical travel are measured in the same units, so a horizontal run and a vertical run can have equal length. Exactly one of runs three, four, five and six has exactly the same length as the run immediately before it on this walk. For every other neighbouring pair of runs, the two lengths clearly differ. The wire's colour, its size on the page, its position on the page, which end carries the block, and the isolated specks scattered in the background all carry no information. Which run has exactly the same length as the run just before it on the walk from the block? Answer with one of: third, fourth, fifth, sixth.
